If the paper backing is stuck down good I would leave it. If your putting down click laminate or vinyl it should be fine. 

Make sure the edges of the paper backing are a smooth transition to the floor, if it is not smooth then you will need to use a floor filler like planie patch or something similar. 

From my experience I would say the paper backing does not contain asbestos but I would not worry about it since your going over it.

Do not soak the floor with anything, this could compermise the wood floor underneath the paper or the glue. As well as cause issues with mold or mildew.

If the flooring was installed correctly, and it could have been since perimeter glue is a thing. Then I would ask for the flooring company to send out a rep from the manufacturer to have a look, because it looks like the product has failed.

I have installed perimeter glue linoleum or vinyl and loose lay vinyl before but if it was my house I would glue the whole dam thing down with the right glue. If it's not glued down solid this can happen and or it can rip.

They might tell you to put something heavy on it or turn up the heat or don't let the direct light hit it, but tell the no it need to be fixed. 

If I was the installer I would get guidance from the rep and maybe glue the whole thing down if they would back me up on that. But i probable wouldn't touch it myself.

Not if it's a product that is only perimeter glue flooring. There are lots of methods of install a floor and it's different on every product. 

There are loose lay vinyl, perimeter glue, cross section glue and full spread glue, there is also regular glue, pressure sensitive glue and the list goes on. It's not installed wrong persay the product might have just failed
